title: The Incarnation of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The incarnation of Christ means that the eternal Son of God took on human flesh and became truly man without ceasing to be truly God. In Jesus, God came near to reveal Himself and redeem sinners.
summary: The incarnation of Christ means that the eternal Son of God took on human flesh and became truly man without ceasing to be truly God. In Jesus, God came near to reveal Himself and redeem sinners.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Word made flesh. In Him, God’s glory, grace, truth, humility, and saving purpose are revealed in real human life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The incarnation is the wonder of the eternal Son entering human history. God did not save from a distance. The Son took on flesh, was born under the law, and came among the people He would redeem.

In becoming man, Christ did not stop being God. He humbled Himself, but He did not surrender His divine identity. The incarnation joins true deity and true humanity in the one person of Jesus Christ.

The incarnation was necessary for salvation. The Savior had to share in flesh and blood to suffer, die, defeat death, and become a merciful and faithful High Priest for His people.

This doctrine also guards the truth of the Gospel. A Christ who only appeared human could not truly stand in our place. A Christ who is not God could not save. The incarnate Son is able to reveal God and redeem humanity.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
The incarnation tells the wounded and distant that God has come near. He did not treat human suffering, weakness, or sin as something beneath His concern. The Son entered our condition to rescue us.

This doctrine also protects worship from vague spirituality. Christians do not worship an idea of divine kindness; they worship the Son who came in the flesh, lived among sinners, and gave Himself for them.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Receive the nearness of God in Christ with worship and faith. Do not treat the incarnation as a seasonal idea only. Let it shape your confidence that Jesus truly understands, truly represents, and truly saves those who come to Him.
